requirements_summary: Media company with ~20M minutes of audio + 3M long-form articles. Primary need: high-precision search over long docs (scene/segment-aware) with reranking to surface authoritative clips. Targets: p95 latency <= 700ms for top-k pipeline under pilot (K=10), cost-per-query target $0.002-0.01 depending on qps, support for retention/residency in NA. Wants two-stage retrieval: dense ANN (existing FAISS) -> cross-encoder reranker (on GPU). Needs VPC/private control plane and KMS integration. Open to Redwood Optimize recommendations for chunk sizes and quantization profiles.
notes:
-- Customer background: archival media house, rights-managed footage + transcripts, heavy legal discovery use-cases.
-- Chunking conversation notes: prefers semantics-aware chunking (scene boundaries, speaker turns) vs fixed 1k token windows. Will run experiments: 512, 1024, 2048 token windows and 'scene' split heuristic. Concern: too small chunks increase index size and retrieval false positives; too large chunks hurt reranker performance.
-- Reranker tuning: currently evaluating cross-encoder BERT-large fine-tuned on pairwise relevance labels (internal) vs distilled cross-encoder for latency. Interested in Redwood's recommendation: cascade reranker (lightweight bi-encoder filter -> heavy cross-encoder rerank top 50).
-- Indexing scale: pilot indexing ~3M documents -> ~12M chunks (estimate). Need guidance on shard sizing, batch-upsert throughput, and warm KV cache behavior for conversational re-rank caching.
-- Latency/cost tradeoffs: customer calculates cost-per-query = (ANN + embed lookup) + (reranker forward passes). Wants cost modeling for 10 qps vs 100 qps; sensitivity to batch sizes and batching latency.
-- Security: must run private control plane; on-prem installer preferred for legal team. Requires KMS integration and 7-year audit log retention for certain assets.
-- Quote from Head of Search: "If we can hit p95 < 700ms with high precision on legacy transcripts we'll sign pilot — but we need a clear cost model for scale."
